papers.title: Polysomnographic Sleep in Idiopathic Nightmares: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: This study conducted a systematic evaluation of polysomnographic differences between individuals with nightmares and healthy controls. Electronic searches of All EBM databases, EMBASE, Web of Science, and MEDLINE identified 14 eligible case-control studies; seven studies involving 112 individuals with nightmares and 112 controls were included in meta-analysis. The meta-analysis of sleep macro-architecture (such as total sleep time, wake after sleep onset, and sleep stage percentages) revealed no significant differences between individuals with nightmares and healthy controls. Furthermore, the limited available data regarding sleep micro-architecture (cyclic alternating patterns (CAP) and power spectral analysis (PSA)) and autonomic measures (heart rate and heart rate variability) in studies not subjected to meta-analysis makes it difficult to draw confident conclusions. Our meta-analysis revealed no significant differences in sleep macro-architecture. This finding highlights the importance of investigating sleep micro-architecture (such as CAP and PSA), which may be relevant to the physiology of nightmares. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and validated in future studies because of the limited available data.

papers.title: Lifespan Trajectories of Resting State Bipolar EEG Power
papers.abstract: Normative trajectories of resting state bipolar EEG power over the lifespan were derived from a sample of 5781 participants from the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism (COGA), a large multi site study, using 12,906 observations from ages 12 through 70. Trajectories were analyzed using the means, variances, and correlations of data in seven frequency bands (from low theta to high beta) and 24 bipolar channels obtained from 17 electrodes of the 10-20 system. In order to make the study more useful for understanding EEG in the general population, only subjects never having an alcohol use disorder (AUD) diagnosis were included in the study. Bipolar EEG data is derived from the differencing of the signals in adjacent electrodes, either in a lateral (left-right) or sagittal (anterior-posterior) orientation; each difference is called a channel. The power values for the individual observations were calculated by standard Fourier transform based methods. In all cases there are sharp decreases in EEG power from ages 12 to the early 20s after which there are number of divergent patterns: general increases in the beta frequencies, and mixed patterns of increase and subsequent decrease in the theta and alpha frequencies. In these characteristics the lifespan trajectories presented here are similar to the monopolar trajectories described in our previous study \citet{Cho2026}. Sagittal and lateral bipolar trajectories are similar within each sex and between sexes; the primary difference is the much lower degree of regional difference in the sagittal trajectories as compared to the lateral trajectories. The pairwise inter-frequency (within channel) correlation trajectories between the four theta and alpha frequency bands and the four high alpha and beta frequency bands at each channel show striking sex differences unlike the corresponding monopolar correlations. There are a number of features in the bipolar power trajectories that suggest that the differencing procedure reduces not only local phase synchrony, but also effects of global and regional phase synchrony present in the monopolar data from which the bipolar signals are derived. The inter-frequency correlations at the individual channels are much higher in the bipolar data than the monopolar data, suggesting that global and regional phase synchrony components retained in the monopolar data have greater frequency specificity than the more purely local components in the bipolar data. Further analyses to examine many other features of the data will be undertaken in our subsequent work.

The differencing procedure in bipolar data appears to reduce global and regional phase synchrony effects, yielding higher inter-frequency correlations than monopolar data.

papers.title: EEG Signatures Support a Shrinking Spotlight of Attention After Errors.
papers.abstract: Errors inhibit attainment of our goals, but there are many ways to get back on track: from increased caution to heightened attention. In this report we examined EEG signatures of control and perception in 21 participants who completed a luminance-varying flanker task. Hierarchical Sequential Sample Modeling with a shrinking spotlight model was used for algorithmic decomposition of post-error adjustments. Control-related changes included a relationship between frontal midline theta power and raised decision threshold, as well as faster drift rate. Yet contrary to our hypothesis, these relationships were not significantly modulated following an error. Perceptual changes elicited by the luminance manipulation scaled with posterior alpha/beta power; both these extrinsic and intrinsic features loaded on an enhanced drift rate. Most importantly, after an error, this relationship between alpha/beta power and drift rate was enhanced. These findings support separate roles of neural systems in adaptive control: midfrontal regions were linked to generic control, whereas sensory-specific mechanisms of attentional adjustment were specifically recruited to boost evidence accumulation when control is needed.

papers.title: Repeated remimazolam sedation for interstitial brachytherapy in cervical cancer: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Evidence regarding repeated remimazolam administration remains limited. We hypothesized that remimazolam would be associated with fewer adverse events than propofol while maintaining stable sedative requirements across three repeated sedation sessions. Patients with cervical cancer undergoing three fractions of interstitial brachytherapy were randomized to propofol or remimazolam. The primary outcome was the proportion of sedation episodes with at least one prespecified intraoperative adverse event across three sessions. Secondary outcomes included sedative dose, hemodynamics, and sleep quality assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS). A total of 100 participants were randomized, of whom 91 completed all three prespecified sedation sessions and were included in the primary per-protocol analysis (46 in the propofol group and 45 in the remimazolam group). Across 138 propofol and 135 remimazolam episodes, overall adverse events were less frequent with remimazolam (17.78% vs. 59.42%; RR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.49; p < 0.001). Respiratory depression (3.70% vs. 26.09%; RR, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.04-0.53; p = 0.004) and hypotension (8.15% vs. 41.30%; RR, 0.20; 95% CI, 0.09-0.42; p < 0.001) were also lower with remimazolam. Remimazolam requirements remained stable across sessions (third vs. first: mean difference, 0.19 mg; 95% CI, -0.78 to 1.15; p = 0.846). No significant between-group differences were observed in PSQI or AIS scores. Across three consecutive sedation sessions for interstitial brachytherapy, remimazolam was associated with fewer respiratory and hemodynamic adverse events than propofol, while sedative requirements remained stable across the three sessions. papers.title: Beyond Snoring, Sleepiness and Surgery: Update on the Prevalent Symptoms of and Treatment Effects in all Age Groups With Pediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: Screening and treatments for pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (pOSA) often use adult symptoms and conventional surgical approaches. This study tested the hypothesis that symptoms and treatment efficacy for OSA differ across age groups. Single-center cohort study of 0 to 18-year-olds who were managed and underwent polysomnography (PSG) in a pediatric-dedicated sleep medicine center from 2020 to 2024. Of 491 children, 489 had pOSA, 57.7% were male, the median age was 6 years old (IQR1-3, 4-9), and 41% already had an adeno- or adenotonsillectomy prior to the PSG. Only 15.6% were obese, and 13.2% had an Epworth Sleepiness Score over 10. Snoring was not the most prevalent nocturnal symptom: restlessness (91.6%), chronic insomnia (86.1%), kicking legs (82.0%), and frequent awakening (78.4%) were all more common. Neurocognitive issues, present in 93.7%, were most commonly mood swings (86.5%) and ADHD (51.9%). Of the 270 without surgery before the PSG, 72.2% (n = 195) were referred, and 173 had surgery. Positive airway pressure (PAP) was prescribed for 240 (49.1%) patients, 176 (73%) of whom had enough CPAP usage to provide machine-estimated apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). After adenotonsillectomy, 27.0% had a post-operative AHI under 5 events per hour, and 73.1% had improvement in neurocognitive issues while that was 94.9% and 87.2% in those using PAP, respectively. After adjusting for age and AHI, PAP had threefold (aOR 3.85, 95%CI 1.39-10.67) higher odds of improving neurocognitive issues than surgery, p = 0.010. The majority of children with pOSA are not tired or obese. Insomnia and restless sleep are more common than snoring. Daytime neurocognitive issues affect almost all children with pOSA and improve with treatment, especially PAP.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances and Sarcopenia in Older Adults: Clinical Associations, Potential Mechanisms, and Management Strategies.
papers.abstract: Sarcopenia is an age-related syndrome characterized by reduced skeletal muscle mass, decreased muscle strength, and impaired physical performance, and is an important contributor to falls, disability, hospitalization, and mortality in older adults. Sleep disturbances, including abnormal sleep duration, poor sleep quality, insomnia, circadian disruption, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), are also highly prevalent in this population and may be associated with poorer physical performance. Accumulating observational evidence suggests an association between sleep disturbances and sarcopenia, although its directionality remains uncertain. This narrative review summarizes current clinical evidence linking sleep disturbances to sarcopenia in older adults, discusses potential biological and behavioral pathways underlying this relationship, and outlines clinically relevant management strategies. A particular focus is the comparison of evidence across sleep domains, sarcopenia components, and study designs, distinguishing clinically defined sarcopenia from individual muscle traits and biological plausibility from demonstrated mediation. Potential pathways involve circadian disruption, neuroendocrine and metabolic dysregulation, chronic inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, although direct mechanistic evidence in older adults remains limited. Sleep assessment and management of clinically identified sleep disturbances may complement exercise and nutritional support, but their effects on sarcopenia outcomes remain uncertain. The available clinical evidence is predominantly observational and often cross-sectional; prospective studies and adequately powered randomized trials in older adults with both conditions are needed to clarify causality and treatment benefits.

papers.title: Distinct sleep and rest-activity profiles according to adjuvant treatment exposure in women treated for breast cancer.
papers.abstract: The associations between adjuvant treatment combinations and sleep-wake processes in women treated for breast cancer remain poorly understood, thereby limiting the development of individualized supportive care. This exploratory study aims to investigate this effect in women treated for breast cancer receiving chemotherapy (CT) combined or not with radio- (RT) and endocrine (ET) therapies on sleep-wake processes and cancer-related fatigue. Sixty-two participants were evaluated (21 patients receiving CT+RT+ET [CT group], 23 patients receiving RT+ET only [nonCT group], and 16 healthy control women [HC group]). Participants completed questionnaires assessing cancer-related fatigue and sleep complaints and wore a wrist actigraph for 72 hours to extract sleep-derived and rest-activity rhythm parameters. GLM served to compare groups when controlling for age and cancer stage. Correlation matrices were computed using Spearman's correlations to evaluate the links between variables in each patient' group. Sleep complaints and cancer-related fatigue did not significantly differ between groups. The CT group had fewer but longer nocturnal awakenings and shorter sleep-onset latency compared to both nonCT and HC groups. The nonCT group had lower dichotomy index-reflecting robustness of the rest-activity rhythm-than the CT group but did not differ significantly from the HCs. Fatigue was negatively correlated with rest-activity rhythm amplitude in the nonCT group. This exploratory study suggests that distinct patterns of sleep-wake parameters may be observed across the treatment exposure- groups (i.e., RT and ET + or - CT). These results should not be interpreted as evidence that treatment exposure itself explains the observed sleep-wake differences and require further investigation to be confirmed. This study was registered at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04391543.

papers.title: Effect of a wearable-based individualised multidomain lifestyle intervention on cognitive and physical function in older adults at risk of decline (INSPIOR): a single-centre, open-label, randomised controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Multidomain lifestyle programmes are the leading preventive approach to cognitive decline, but they rely on intensive face-to-face delivery that is hard to scale. We assessed whether an automated, wearable-based multidomain programme of activity, sleep, and optional nutrition prompts changed cognitive and physical function in at-risk older adults. INSPIOR was a 6-month, single-centre, open-label, randomised controlled trial in Kashiwa, Japan. Adults aged 65-92 years with low body-mass index, pre-frailty, frailty, or sarcopenia-related decline were randomly assigned 1:1, in permuted blocks of four and without stratification, to the Fitbit-based intervention or an assessment-only control; allocation was not concealed and outcome assessors were not masked. Co-primary outcomes were the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Trail Making Test (TMT), and skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), with no pre-specified hierarchy or multiplicity adjustment; analyses used intention-to-treat analysis of covariance with multiple imputation. This trial was registered with UMIN-CTR, UMIN000052707, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06135740. Between Nov 8, 2023, and Jul 31, 2024, 355 participants were randomly assigned to the intervention group (n = 178) or control group (n = 177); all were analysed. Adjusted between-group differences were 0·58 MoCA points (95% CI 0·03-1·13; p = 0·039; Holm-adjusted p = 0·12), 0·16 s (-5·07 to 5·40; p = 0·95) for TMT-A, 5·59 s (-3·88 to 15·05; p = 0·25) for TMT-B, and -0·01 kg/m2 (-0·09 to 0·07; p = 0·88) for SMI. Mild skin irritation and dietary-recording stress occurred; no serious adverse event was intervention-related. The intervention was associated with a small difference in a global cognitive screening score that did not survive multiplicity adjustment and is of uncertain clinical significance; the other two showed none. Larger, longer, masked trials are needed. University of Tokyo-NH Foods Collaborative Research Programme, Google, Mitsui Fudosan.

papers.title: Modulating stress and sleep through a multi-compound dietary supplement: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Stress and poor sleep are prevalent public health concerns that negatively impact well-being and daily functioning. Although adaptogens and sleep-focused supplements have separately demonstrated potential benefits, few studies have examined combined effects, particularly in healthy populations. Therefore, this study evaluated the impact of morning adaptogens, evening sleep-focused supplements, and their combination on stress, mood, and subjective and objective sleep quality. Using a double-blind, placebo-controlled design, 103 healthy physically active adults (F = 53; age = 34.8 ± 9.6 yrs; BMI = 24.0 ± 2.7 kg/m2) were randomized to one of four treatment groups: 1) AMPM (n = 25): active morning (AM) and active evening (PM); 2) AM (n = 26): active AM and placebo PM; 3) PM (n = 25): placebo AM and active PM; and 4) PL (n = 27): placebo AM and placebo PM). The AM group contained 600 mg ashwagandha and 300 mg Rhodiola rosea (R. rosea). The PM group contained 2 g Magnesium L-threonate (MgT) (delivering 145 mg of magnesium), 200 mg L-theanine, and 50 mg apigenin. The total study duration was four weeks, consisting of one baseline week, two weeks of supplementation, and one washout week. Participants completed daily stress questionnaires and weekly questionnaires on perceived stress, affect, and subjective sleep (Patient-Reported Outcome Measurement Information System (PROMIS), and monthly subjective sleep (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) at baseline and post-washout. Objective sleep data were collected nightly using a wearable sleep monitoring device. Data were analyzed using baseline-adjusted linear mixed-effects models with alpha set at 0.05. Tukey-adjusted post hoc comparisons were performed, and effect sizes are reported as partial eta squared (η2) and Cohen's d (d). The AM group showed a decrease in weekly perceived stress (p = 0.034; η2 = 0.020), whereas there were no differences in daily stress (p < 0.05). For positive affect, there was a significant effect in the AM group at the end of the cessation period (p = 0.003; d = 1.68), which continued to increase, whereas the AMPM group showed a decrease (p = 0.009; d = 0.16). The AM group showed a decrease in subjective sleep-related impairments (p = 0.032, d = 2.74) and in objective wake after sleep onset (p = 0.047, η2 = 0.020). PSQI subjective sleep quality was significantly improved in the AM group compared with the AMPM group (mean difference = 0.66 AU, p < 0.001, d = 1.45). Morning supplementation with adaptogens (ashwagandha and R. rosea) was associated with improvements in subjective stress, sleep quality, and positive affect following 14 days in healthy physically active adults as compared to the placebo product. Minimal effects on other outcomes may reflect limited benefits in healthy individuals over a short supplementation period. Future research should investigate longer interventions and populations with greater baseline stress and sleep disturbance.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic patterns of electroencephalography (EEG)-derived aperiodic activity across schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar, and depressive disorders: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: Aperiodic electroencephalographic activity is proposed as a scalable marker of cortical population dynamics relevant to excitation-inhibition balance. However, it remains unclear whether aperiodic parameters represent disorder-specific abnormalities or context-sensitive indices of clinically relevant brain states. Consistent with systematic-review guidelines and a prospectively registered protocol, Ovid databases and PubMed were searched from inception through February 9, 2026, with updated manual searching conducted through July 14, 2026. Peer-reviewed studies reporting electroencephalography-derived aperiodic parameters in adults with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, major depressive disorder, treatment-resistant depression, and/or bipolar disorder were eligible. Studies lacking aperiodic outcomes or separable findings for eligible diagnoses were excluded. Two reviewers independently conducted study screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessments. Findings were synthesized narratively by diagnosis, recording context, and parameter. Thirty articles (N = 2298 aggregate participants) spanning cross-sectional, longitudinal, and interventional designs were included. Findings in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders were heterogeneous, with several studies reporting steeper slopes, higher offsets, or reduced temporal flexibility relative to healthy controls. Task-related and dynamic measures often showed greater clinical relevance than static resting-state parameters. Studies of major depressive disorder and treatment-resistant depression more consistently reported flatter slopes and reduced offsets, particularly in central and posterior regions, with evidence from sleep and intracranial recordings. Aperiodic parameters were sensitive to treatment-related modulation, although the direction of change differed across interventions. Bipolar disorder evidence was limited, and methodological heterogeneity precluded quantitative synthesis. Aperiodic electroencephalographic activity may be more informative as a context-sensitive, within-subject marker of cortical state and treatment-related change than a fixed diagnostic signature. Methodological harmonization and direct physiological validation remain necessary before clinical implementation.

The authors conclude that aperiodic parameters may be more informative as context-sensitive within-subject markers of cortical state and treatment change than as fixed diagnostic signatures.

papers.title: Cognitive impairment in idiopathic intracranial hypertension: A conceptual framework and therapeutic implications.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment is an increasingly recognized but poorly understood manifestation of idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH). Although deficits in attention, executive functioning, memory, processing speed, and reaction time have been reported, the characteristics, trajectory, and underlying mechanisms of cognitive dysfunction remain incompletely defined. Interpretation of the literature is limited by heterogeneity in study design, variability in neurocognitive assessment methods, and the absence of standardized cognitive outcome measures. Consequently, cognitive morbidity is overlooked in clinical practice and is not incorporated into treatment decision-making, which remains centered around visual outcomes and papilledema. In this narrative review, we synthesize evidence from IIH studies and related disease models to examine the putative mechanisms underlying cognitive dysfunction and propose a conceptual framework for its pathogenesis. Cognitive dysfunction in IIH may arise through interactions between elevated intracranial pressure, cerebral venous hypertension, symptom-related amplifiers including chronic headache, sleep disturbance, pulsatile tinnitus, and psychiatric comorbidity, and broader biological and socioeconomic modifiers influencing cognitive vulnerability and recovery. This framework integrates current evidence and identifies potential pathways linking IIH to cognitive impairment. Improved understanding of the cognitive effects of IIH may help improve recognition of cognitive dysfunction in clinical care. Recognition of cognition as a clinically meaningful and potentially treatment-responsive outcome may help inform future studies evaluating whether cognition has a role in treatment selection, particularly in patients without papilledema, in whom disease burden may currently be underestimated.

It argues that cognition should be recognized as a clinically meaningful and potentially treatment-responsive outcome in IIH, particularly in patients without papilledema.

papers.title: Understanding sleep-related quality of life in caregivers of people with traumatic brain injury.
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationships among measures of subjective and objective sleep-related quality of life (SRQOL), health-related quality of life (HRQOL), and care recipient functioning in caregivers of persons with traumatic brain injury (PwTBI). This secondary analysis utilized data from a 6-month randomized controlled trial conducted at two academic medical centers. The sample included 257 informal caregivers of PwTBI, who completed monthly survey assessments and continuous wrist actigraphy monitoring. Objective SRQOL was measured as average sleep duration and variability via actigraphy; subjective SRQOL was measured using PROMIS Fatigue and Sleep-Related Impairment. HRQOL was assessed with established caregiver and general health measures. Caregivers (n = 228) slept a mean of 6.8 hr per night, with a mean within-month night-to-night variability of approximately 1.4 hr. Objective and subjective SRQOL were weakly correlated (r = -.02-.28), and neither was strongly associated with care recipient functioning. However, subjective sleep impairment and fatigue were highly correlated (r = .84) and showed moderate to high associations with most measures of HRQOL (r > .40). Linear mixed-effects models indicated that greater between-subjects sleep variability, but not sleep duration, was associated with worse global physical and mental health. These findings highlight the need to further examine the relationship between sleep variability and HRQOL in caregivers of PwTBI. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Environmental circadian disruption alters rhythmicity of clock and epigenetic gene expression in SKH-1 female mouse livers.
papers.abstract: Endogenous circadian rhythms are primarily entrained by environmental cues that are used to regulate the function of cells and peripheral tissues throughout the body. We found that disrupted light schedules - reflective of shift work conditions - demonstrated impaired gene expression throughout the 24-h day in core clock and epigenetically regulated genes. Dysregulated expression in these genes has been independently detected in the etiology of sleep-related diseases, suggesting epigenetic regulation as a potential mechanistic link between circadian disruption and health outcomes. Because of this, we hypothesized that epigenetic regulatory factors are circadian expressed and can be dysregulated by environmental circadian disruption. In this study, we show rhythmic expression of both core clock and epigenetic genes in female SKH-1 mouse livers under normal circadian conditions and the subsequent effect of disrupted clocks thereafter. To address our hypothesis, we measured relative gene expression patterns in female mouse livers under healthy and disrupted clock conditions. In 5 of the 8 core clock genes (Cry1, Cry2, Npas2, Nr1d1, Per2), there was a significant loss of rhythmic expression. All active demethylases and Zfp57 experienced a loss of rhythmicity due to clock disruption, while both de novo DNMTs, Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b, displayed a slight damping of rhythmicity in disrupted clock mice.

papers.title: Predicting One-Year CPAP Adherence and Use Trajectories Utilizing Baseline and Early Use Data
papers.abstract: Introduction Maintaining long-term positive airway pressure (CPAP) adherence is a major challenge when treating obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). We evaluated factors associated with one-year CPAP adherence and developed models predicting Month-12 adherence and CPAP-use trajectories. Methods CPAP-naive adults with OSA (apnea-hypopnea index[≥]5) at Kaiser Permanente Southern California with 364-day observation period were analyzed (development/internal-validation cohort, n=14,906; temporal holdout, n=1,676). Logistic regression evaluated baseline associations with Month-12 adherence (mean[≥]4 hours/night during days 331-360). XGBoost models utilized baseline features (clinical, sleep-study, questionnaire data), early CPAP data (days 1-7), or combined to predict long-term CPAP use. A latent-class model identified trajectories over days 8-364. Predictive models were evaluated in both random and temporal holdouts. Results About one-third (34.6%) of the primary cohort (49.7{+/-}13.8 years, 63.2% male) were adherent during Month-12. Higher AHI and longer self-reported sleep duration favored adherence while greater comorbidity burden, depression, and substance-use disorder were associated with lower adherence. In held-out testing, adherence prediction using baseline features yielded an AUROC of 0.678. Using CPAP-only data, AUROCs were higher from 0.787 with seven days of usage data to 0.816 and 0.854 with 14 and 30 days. Models combining CPAP and baseline features increased Day-7 AUROC to 0.810. We identified four one-year trajectories: Early-Decliners (42.9%), Gradual-Decliners (17.4%), Stable-Moderate (19.0%), Stable-High (20.7%). Models predicting patient trajectory revealed macro-average AUROCs of 0.619, 0.756, and 0.770 for baseline, CPAP-only, and combined models. Conclusion Baseline predictors may identify strategies for adherence support, while early CPAP data substantially improved predictive performance. These models may guide personalized follow-up but should not restrict CPAP access. External and implementation validation are needed.

Baseline features alone yielded an AUROC of 0.678, while using 7, 14, or 30 days of CPAP data improved AUROCs to 0.787, 0.816, and 0.854; four one-year trajectories were identified, with early CPAP data substantially improving predictive performance for both adherence and trajectory.

papers.title: Potential effect of replacing sedentary behavior with physical activity on the risk of atrial fibrillation: results from the UK Biobank and REGARDS study
papers.abstract: Background Sedentary behavior (SB) has been associated with cardiovascular disease risk, independent of physical activity (PA) and sleep. However, the effect of replacing SB with PA or sleep on atrial fibrillation (AF) risk remains unclear. Methods We studied 86,096 participants from the United Kingdom Biobank (UKB) and 5,777 from the United States (US) REasons for Geographic And Racial Differences in Stroke (REGARDS) prospective cohort studies who were free of AF at baseline and had valid accelerometry data. The two cohorts were included to evaluate the consistency of associations across distinct populations in the UK and the US, two regions with a high burden of AF. Daily time spent in light PA (LPA), moderate to vigorous PA (MVPA), and SB were derived from accelerometer recordings; sleep was accelerometer-derived in UKB and self-reported in REGARDS. Incident AF was identified using ICD-10 codes (I48.x) listed as either a primary diagnosis, secondary diagnosis, or cause of death through hospital and death registry data linkage in UKB and in a follow-up visit through electrocardiogram and self-reported medical history in REGARDS. Isotemporal substitution models were used to examine replacing 30 minutes of SB with LPA or MVPA in both cohorts and with sleep in UKB on the outcome of incident AF. Results Among the UKB participants [57% female, mean age 56.0 (SD 7.8) years, 98% White race], 4,035 AF cases were identified during a median of 7.9 years of follow-up. Replacing 30 minutes of SB with PA was associated with a slightly lower risk of AF in the minimally adjusted models but the associations were attenuated after full adjustment (LPA: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.95-1.02; MVPA: HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.99-1.02). The REGARDS participants had an average age of 63 (SD 8.3) years, 55% female, 31% Black and 69% White adults, with 486 AF cases identified. Fully adjusted substitution of 30 minutes of SB with MVPA was associated with lower AF odds (OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.63-1.01), whereas LPA showed no association. In UKB, replacing SB with sleep was not associated with AF risk. The magnitude of the association of MVPA substitution with AF appeared stronger among REGARDS participants aged [≥]65 years and those reporting <7 hours/day of sleep. Conclusion Replacing SB with moderate or higher intensity PA may decrease AF risk. In REGARDS, these substitutions appeared to benefit older individuals and those reporting shorter sleep duration. These findings highlight the potential benefit of reducing sedentarism to lower AF burden, warranting validation in future studies.

papers.title: Differences of physical activity, sleep quality and depressive symptoms in patients with diabetes and non-diabetes undergoing maintenance hemodialysis in Xi'an, China: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: To compare the physical activity, sleep quality and depressive symptoms between patients with diabetes and non-diabetes undergoing maintenance hemodialysis, and identify associated influencing factors. A descriptive cross-sectional design was adopted. Maintenance hemodialysis patients were enrolled from two hemodialysis centers in Xi'an, China between April and May 2022. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected, with physical activity assessed via Human Activity Profile, sleep quality via Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and depressive symptoms via Beck Depression Inventory-II. Of 286 participants, 113 had diabetes and 173 did not. Diabetic patients had lower adjusted activity scores (40.07 ± 22.94 vs. 55.94 ± 21.35, P < 0.01), higher PSQI global scores (9.04 ± 4.48 vs. 7.15 ± 4.47, P < 0.01), and higher BDI-II scores (17.32 ± 10.75 vs. 12.95 ± 9.26, P < 0.01) than non-diabetic patients. Multivariate logistic regression showed that age (OR = 1.02, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.04) and BDI-II score (OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.07) were positively associated with diabetes, whereas AAS (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.97, 0.99) and MHD duration (OR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.98, 1.00) were negatively associated. Diabetic patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis exhibit poorer physical activity levels, sleep quality, and depressive symptoms compared with non-diabetic counterparts. Accordingly, routine combined screening of physical activity, sleep disturbance and depressive symptoms should be embedded into daily dialysis nursing.

papers.title: Effects of Perioperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine Spray on Clinical Outcomes of Pulsed Radiofrequency in Patients with Zoster-Associated Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effects of perioperative intranasal dexmedetomidine spray on hemodynamic stability, postoperative analgesia and sleep quality in patients with zoster-associated pain (ZAP) undergoing pulsed radiofrequency (PRF), and assess its clinical efficacy and safety. A single-center, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled trial was conducted. Sixty-eight ZAP patients receiving dorsal root ganglion PRF were randomly assigned (1:1) to the dexmedetomidine (Dex) group or control group. The Dex group received intranasal dexmedetomidine 40 μg 30 min preoperatively, followed by 40 μg twice daily for 3 postoperative days; the control group received equal-volume normal saline at matched time points. Perioperative mean arterial pressure (MAP) and heart rate (HR) were recorded. Pain intensity (VAS) and sleep quality (PSQI) were assessed at baseline and on postoperative days 1, 3, 7 and 14. The primary outcome was change in MAP from baseline to PRF treatment stage. Linear mixed-effects models were used for longitudinal analyses. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups (all P>0.05). The Dex group showed significantly smaller MAP and HR fluctuations during puncture, nerve stimulation and PRF treatment (group × time interaction, all P<0.001). VAS and PSQI scores were markedly lower in the Dex group at all postoperative time points (all P<0.001 after Bonferroni correction). No severe adverse events occurred; mild-to-moderate transient bradycardia and hypotension in the Dex group required no specific intervention. Perioperative intranasal dexmedetomidine spray effectively stabilizes perioperative hemodynamics, improves postoperative analgesia and sleep quality in ZAP patients undergoing PRF, with no serious safety signals observed in this study population. It provides evidence for optimized perioperative management strategies in this population. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500098608, first posted 11/03/2025.

papers.title: Vanillin alleviates circadian disruption-induced cognitive impairment: involvement of gut microbiota alterations and tryptophan metabolism.
papers.abstract: Circadian disruption (CD) is an important risk factor for cognitive impairment and neurodegenerative diseases, potentially through disturbances in tryptophan (TRP) metabolism. This study investigated the protective effects of orally administered vanillin in a mouse model of CD. CD impaired spatial learning and recognition memory, whereas vanillin improved cognitive performance and corrected abnormal changes in TRP-related metabolites, including tryptophan, kynurenine (KYN), and kynurenic acid (KYNA). Vanillin also modulated the composition and diversity of the gut microbiota, enhanced intestinal barrier function, and improved immune homeostasis. Immunofluorescence staining and western blot analysis further showed that vanillin regulated hippocampal proteins associated with neuronal and synaptic function and reduced astrocyte activation. These findings suggest that vanillin alleviates CD-induced cognitive impairment, accompanied by alterations in gut microbiota composition, TRP-kynurenine metabolism, intestinal barrier function, and neuroinflammatory responses.

papers.title: Boder's dyslexia subtypes as a severity continuum with a definitional route axis - A behavioural companion to harmonised qEEG cross-spectra.
papers.abstract: Developmental dyslexia is classically divided into Boder's dysphonetic (DD), dyseidetic (DYD) and mixed (MD) subtypes, assigned by direct reading-and-spelling testing. Its computerised Italian adaptation, the Direct Test of Reading and Spelling (DTRS), assigns the subtype algorithmically from the reading quotient and the percentage of correctly spelt known and unknown words. Using the same source clinical cohort and the same stable and sparse regression classifier (SSRC) as our companion, we asked whether the subtypes form natural clusters or lie on a continuum, and whether reading-time (severity) or qualitative-error (route) information discriminates them. We analysed one DTRS assessment each from 520 children (378 DD, 41 DYD, 101 MD), deriving reading-time indices, including a severity/fluency index (SFI), and Boder's error taxonomies for reading and spelling. Subtype structure was probed with Gaussian-mixture clustering (adjusted Rand index against clinical labels) and Hartigan's dip test; discrimination with the SSRC and robust ROC under participant-level Monte-Carlo cross-validation, with subsampling stability intervals (5th-95th percentile over 300 iterations). Full-sample pairwise AUCs were additionally evaluated with percentile bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (10,000 subject-level resamples of the full-sample classifier scores) and label-permutation tests (10,000 permutations, one-sided and Bonferroni-corrected within each model). No feature space yielded label-aligned mixture solutions (adjusted Rand index ≈ 0); SFI was unimodal (dip p = 0.36). Reading-time indices separated the severity contrast (DD vs MD, stable AUC 0.73 [0.66-0.80]; p < 0.001) but were weak and non-significant for the route contrast (DYD vs DD, 0.58 [0.47-0.69]; p = 0.543, non-significant); reading qualitative errors showed a weak route signal (0.61 [0.50-0.73]; p = 0.062) that did not reach Bonferroni-corrected significance. Unknown-word spelling, the basis of the diagnostic algorithm, separated DD from DYD almost perfectly (0.94-0.98), but partialling out unknown-word accuracy collapsed this to 0.60: the separation is definitional. The severity contrast was likewise definitional: the reading quotient alone separated DD from MD at 0.86, and residualising the reading-time indices on the reading quotient within each training fold reduced the DD-MD AUC from 0.73 to 0.50. In the EEG subsample, no behavioural classifier separated DD from DYD significantly (TIME: 0.52 [0.31-0.75], p = 0.41; ERR: weak and non-significant 0.62 [0.41-0.81], p = 0.15), whereas qEEG cross-spectral connectivity did so at 0.85 in the published qEEG sample of 227 children (169 DD, 18 DYD, 40 MD; Chiarenza et al., 2026). No evidence for natural clusters emerged with the present methods: the subtypes behave as overlapping regions of graded continuous distributions. Both axes of Boder's scheme are threshold-defined - severity by the reading quotient, route by unknown-word spelling - and both are continuously distributed. Once the defining variable is removed, reading dynamics carry no residual severity signal (0.50) and independent behaviour carries only a faint route signal (0.58-0.61); the route distinction is clearest in brain connectivity, which predicts the behaviourally defined labels rather than independently validating a latent route construct. Together, the two papers advance a dimensional, mechanism-aware account of dyslexia subtyping.

papers.title: The Role of Lifestyle Medicine in Shaping and Supporting Successful Aging.
papers.abstract: Within gerontology, various theoretical perspectives on what it means to age successfully have emerged over recent decades (5) and garnered empirical support. Similarly, within medicine and related healthcare fields, research and practice have focused on healthy living in terms of physical health, mental health, and well-being. In recent years, the practice of Lifestyle Medicine (nutrition, physical activity, stress management, restorative sleep, social connection, and avoidance of risky substances) has emerged to describe the role of such lifestyle factors on health. The present article proposes a pathway to integrate lifestyle medicine with successful aging. We take a holistic approach to develop a model that merges the foundational pillars of lifestyle medicine with the principles of successful aging. This new approach to exploring the linkages between the principles of lifestyle medicine and the essential components of successful aging highlights how proactive behavioral health strategies related to nutrition, exercise, sleep, stress, and substances could play a role in fostering optimal aging in cognitive and physical functioning and disease prevention, thereby potentially yielding more positive outcomes for aging well.

papers.title: Respiration and individual differences shape behavioral and inter-brain synchronization
papers.abstract: Humans coordinate their actions while their bodies and brains synchronize in social interactions, yet how behavioral, physiological, and neural dynamics interact during interpersonal coordination remains largely unknown. We investigated how respiration and individual differences influence behavioral and inter-brain synchrony in a musical synchronization task, which requires precise temporal alignment. Eighty-eight individuals first produced a familiar melody at their most comfortable rate to measure their spontaneous production rate (SPR). They then synchronized the melody with a randomly assigned unfamiliar partner under natural (unpaced), instructed in-phase, and instructed anti-phase breathing conditions, while hyperscanning 64-channel electroencephalography (EEG), respiration, auditory-motor timing, and perceived social connectedness were recorded. Relative to natural respiration, both in-phase and anti-phase breathing increased inter-brain phase-locking and perceived social closeness but reduced behavioral synchrony; the instructed respiratory phase relationship was mirrored in their inter-brain relative phase. Differences in phase of respiratory cycles (inhalation and exhalation) also influenced coordination: Inhalation was associated with stronger inter-brain synchronization but less precise and stable behavioral coordination than was exhalation. Moreover, Individual differences influenced coordination: Partners with the faster SPR consistently preceded the slower partners and exhibited an alpha-band inter-brain phase advance in synchronization, whereas dyads with similar SPR showed greater behavioral synchrony and smaller inter-brain phase difference. Our findings identify respiration as a previously overlooked factor that organizes behavioral and neural synchronization, while individual intrinsic rhythms constrain how interacting partners align in time. Together, these findings reveal a dynamic interplay between the rhythms of the body and brain during human social interactions.

papers.title: Diabetes Insipidus as a Rare Complication of Metastatic Breast Cancer With Pituitary Metastases.
papers.abstract: Diabetes insipidus (DI) is a rare but significant and life-threatening complication of metastatic breast cancer, typically arising when cancer spreads to the pituitary gland. This condition results from impaired secretion or action of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or arginine vasopressin (AVP), leading to symptoms including excessive urination and thirst. The posterior lobe of the pituitary and the infundibulum are most susceptible to metastatic involvement due to their direct arterial blood supply, making them more accessible to circulating tumor cells. This phenomenon explains why DI can be a manifestation of pituitary metastases. We report the case of a patient who presented with a five-week history of projectile vomiting, dizziness, blurred vision, headache, insatiable thirst, and nocturia. She reported urinating up to 12 times at night such that she struggled to sleep and would end up having daytime lethargy and fatigue. Biochemical evaluation demonstrated hyperosmolar serum, low urine osmolality, and low urine sodium, consistent with central DI. MRI revealed a pituitary stalk and suprasellar metastases with multiple new cerebral and cerebellar lesions. The patient underwent a desmopressin challenge leading to rapid improvement in polyuria and an increase in urine osmolality. Desmopressin confirmed an intact renal response, establishing the diagnosis of cranial DI secondary to pituitary metastases. Despite symptomatic benefit, her overall condition deteriorated due to progressive intracranial and systemic disease. She subsequently received whole-brain radiotherapy and palliative care but died three months after the diagnosis of DI. This case highlights central DI as a rare but clinically important manifestation of pituitary metastases in metastatic breast cancer. Prompt recognition and endocrine replacement, particularly with desmopressin, can provide meaningful symptomatic relief even when prognosis remains poor. Early multidisciplinary involvement, including endocrinology, oncology, radiology, and palliative care, is essential for optimizing quality of life in such complex cases.

papers.title: Coblation intracapsular tonsillectomy outcomes in paediatric obstructive sleep disordered breathing: A Singapore study.
papers.abstract: Coblation intracapsular tonsillectomy (ICT) may offer a more favourable post-operative morbidity profile compared with extracapsular tonsillectomy for paediatric obstructive sleep-disordered breathing (oSDB). Data from the Singapore paediatric population remain limited. This study examines the outcomes of coblation ICT in children with oSDB at a tertiary centre in Singapore. This was a single-centre prospective cohort study of 102 consecutive children aged 21 months to 15 years undergoing coblation ICT for oSDB (April-October 2023). Concurrent adenoidectomy was performed in 98.0% of patients. Primary outcomes included complications and disease-specific quality of life (QoL) via the Obstructive Sleep Apnea-18 Quality of Life (OSA-18) questionnaire (where higher scores indicate greater symptom burden and poorer quality of life), assessed pre-operatively and at 3 months. Secondary outcomes included pain, analgesia, diet, and snoring resolution. No post-operative haemorrhage or major complications occurred. All 102 patients completed a 3-month review. The median OSA-18 score improved significantly from 74 (interquartile range [IQR] 54-89) to 29.5 (IQR 23-40) post-operatively (P<0.001), representing a shift from the moderate to the minimal impact band. The mean change of 39.3 points exceeded twice the published minimal clinically important difference (standardised response mean 2.17). Perceived QoL score improved from median 5 (IQR 4-6.6) to 8 (IQR 8-9) (P<0.001). At 3 months, 82.4% had no snoring. Postoperative pain was mild, with 75.5% requiring analgesia for 3 days or fewer. In this uncontrolled single-arm cohort, coblation ICT with concurrent adenoidectomy was associated with low morbidity and clinically meaningful improvements in caregiver-reported outcomes. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant further investigation through multicentre comparative studies with longer follow-up.

papers.title: Spiritual well-being, sleep quality as a buffer against burnout and in increasing professional fulfillment among healthcare professionals in the United Arab Emirates.
papers.abstract: Burnout is a growing concern among healthcare professionals (HCPs) in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Emerging evidence suggests that sleep quality and spiritual well-being may buffer against burnout and enhance professional fulfilment. This study explores the relationship between sleep disturbance, spiritual well-being, and burnout among HCPs in the UAE. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 661 healthcare professionals across the UAE. Validated instruments were used to measure sleep quality, circadian regularity, spiritual well-being, burnout, and professional fulfilment. Data was analyzed using correlation and regression models to identify predictive factors. Poor sleep quality and irregular circadian patterns were significantly associated with higher levels of burnout. Conversely, higher spiritual well-being showed a strong negative correlation with burnout and a positive association with professional fulfilment. Multivariate analysis identified sleep regularity and spiritual well-being as significant independent predictors of both burnout and professional fulfilment. Sleep quality and spiritual well-being play a protective role against burnout and contribute to greater professional fulfilment among healthcare professionals in the UAE. These findings highlight the importance of addressing sleep issues and nurturing spiritual well-being to mitigate burnout and enhance job satisfaction among healthcare professionals, thereby facilitating targeted interventions for improved occupational health and well-being.

papers.title: PSYCHONEUROLOGICAL THERAPY FOR POST-COVID SYNDROME: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF METHODS AND CLINICAL EFFECTIVENESS.
papers.abstract: Post-COVID syndrome has emerged as a major global health issue characterized by long-lasting psychoneurological symptoms, including cognitive impairment, anxiety, depression, sleep disturbances, and fatigue. These symptoms can persist regardless of the severity of the initial SARS-CoV-2 infection and often result in long-term functional limitations. The purpose of this review was to summarize current evidence on psychoneurological therapeutic approaches used to manage post-COVID syndrome and evaluate their clinical effectiveness. A structured literature review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, MEDLINE, and Google Scholar. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and clinical reports published up to 2024 that examined pharmacological, psychotherapeutic, physical, complementary, or neuromodulation-based treatments for adults with persistent psychoneurological symptoms after COVID-19. The review followed standard ethical practices for narrative reviews; no new human or animal data were collected, and therefore ethical approval or CTRI registration was not required. Findings were synthesized narratively by therapy category. The review identified consistent evidence supporting the efficacy of multiple therapeutic modalities. Pharmacological agents including SSRIs, SNRIs, anxiolytics, and nootropics reduced anxiety, depression, and cognitive dysfunction. Psychotherapeutic methods such as cognitive behavioral therapy, psychodynamic therapy, and mindfulness-based interventions improved emotional regulation and coping. Physical rehabilitation, aerobic exercise, and breathing practices enhanced endurance and reduced fatigue. Complementary approaches (e.g., acupuncture, massage) provided additional symptom relief. Neuromodulation techniques, including transcranial magnetic stimulation and electroconvulsive therapy, demonstrated benefits in treatment-resistant cases. Psychoneurological therapy for post-COVID syndrome requires a multimodal approach that integrates pharmacological, psychological, physical, and neuromodulatory interventions. Current evidence suggests that individualized, combined strategies are most effective for improving cognitive, emotional, and functional outcomes. Further research is needed to optimize treatment protocols and evaluate long-term effectiveness.

papers.title: PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING AMONG MEDICAL STUDENTS AT FIVE UNIVERSITIES IN TBILISI, GEORGIA: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY OF PERCEIVED STRESS, ANXIETY, AND SLEEP QUALITY.
papers.abstract: Medical students carry a heavier psychological burden than the general student population, and data from Georgia and the South Caucasus region are scarce. The present study aimed to describe levels of perceived stress, anxiety, and sleep disturbance among medical students at five universities in Tbilisi, Georgia, and to compare these outcomes across years of undergraduate medical training. A cross-sectional observational study enrolled 300 medical students from five universities, all located in Tbilisi, Georgia, using stratified purposive sampling rather than random selection (n = 60 per institution; n = 50 per year of study). Data were collected face-to-face during March-April 2026 using the English-language versions of three validated self-report instruments: the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Analyses included Pearson correlations, independent-samples t-tests, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey post-hoc comparisons. Ethics approval was obtained from the Research Development and Support Department of Georgian American University (No. #ethc-00012026). The mean PSS-10 score was 26.20 (SD=8.19); 96.3% of students fell in the moderate-to-high stress range. The mean GAD-7 score was 13.45 (SD=5.72); 73.7% met criteria for moderate-to-severe anxiety. A total of 58.0% reported fairly or very bad sleep quality. All three outcomes were significantly intercorrelated: PSS-10 vs. GAD-7 (r=0.736, P<0.001); PSS-10 vs. PSQI disturbance (r=0.561, P<0.001). Senior students (years 4-6) reported significantly higher stress than junior students (years 1-3): t(298)=-5.379, P<0.001, Cohen's d=0.62. One-way ANOVA showed higher scores in successive years of study: F(5,294)=8.220, P<0.001, η²=0.123, with the highest mean in year 6 (29.84). Psychological distress was highly prevalent in this sample, and stress scores were higher in later years of study. Year 3, when students move from preclinical to clinical training, marked the point at which scores began to rise. Because the sample was purposive and limited to Tbilisi, the findings should not be generalized to all medical students in Georgia. Within these limits, the results support routine mental health screening and stronger support services at the participating universities.

papers.title: Effect of early regional anesthesia on postoperative cognitive function and the perioperative stress response in patients with hip fractures: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Whether early application of anterior iliopsoas muscle space block (AIMSB) impacts postoperative cognitive function remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare the incidence of postoperative delirium (POD) among patients who received AIMSB at different time points. This prospective, single-blind, randomized trial enrolled 79 patients aged ≥65 years hospitalized for primary unilateral total hip arthroplasty (THA) due to hip fractures (December 2022 to February 2024). All patients underwent spinal anesthesia. Participants were randomized to receive AIMSB either the day before surgery (D group, n = 39) or one hour before surgery (H group, n = 40). The primary outcome was the incidence of POD within 7 days. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores at specified intervals, time to first rescue analgesia, cumulative opioid consumption, motor function recovery time, hospital discharge time, sleep quality, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), and laboratory tests. Seventy-six patients completed the study per protocol. POD incidence was 8.1% (3/37) in the day-before-surgery group and 12.8% (5/39) in the hour-before-surgery group (risk difference, -4.7%; 95% CI [-18.4% to 9.0%]; P = 0.71). At 6 hours postoperatively, resting pain scores (2.46 ± 0.80 vs. 2.95 ± 1.21, P = 0.043) and movement-evoked pain scores (3.24 ± 0.83 vs. 3.79 ± 1.17, P = 0.021) were lower in the D group; however, these differences did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. In an exploratory post-hoc analysis, the IL-6 curve area under the curve was 0.895 (95% CI [0.784-0.998]) this finding requires prospective validation. Among elderly patients undergoing THA for hip fracture, performing AIMSB one day preoperatively, compared to one hour preoperatively, did not significantly reduce the incidence of POD. An exploratory analysis suggested a transient early postoperative pain benefit, that did not survive multiplicity correction. These findings warrant further investigation in larger, appropriately powered trials.

papers.title: Navigating the storm: A qualitative research on contributing factors to diabetes burnout in young adults with type 1 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Diabetes burnout is a serious and often overlooked condition marked by emotional exhaustion, detachment, and a sense of helplessness in managing diabetes. This qualitative content analysis study seeks to uncover the underlying factors that contribute to the onset and persistence of diabetes burnout. Understanding these factors is essential for informing targeted interventions and supportive policies to improve the well-being of individuals living with Type 1 diabetes. Eleven adults with T1D in Shahrekord, Iran, were recruited using purposive sampling to ensure diverse perspectives. Fourteen semi-structured interviews (50-60 minutes each) were conducted in Persian, with two participants completing follow-up sessions. Interviews were recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using Elo and Kyngäs's three-step process: open coding, categorization, and abstraction. Trustworthiness was ensured through prolonged engagement, peer debriefing, member checking, and application of Lincoln and Guba's criteria. Qualitative analysis revealed four interrelated themes contributing to burnout: (1) disruptions in self-management routines (e.g., sleep, exercise, diet); (2) external stressors and resource limitations (e.g., economic instability, healthcare access, medication shortages); (3) fluctuations in physical and emotional well-being; and (4) the role of interpersonal and social support. Many of these challenges were exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, which disrupted healthcare routines and increased psychosocial stress. Participants likened their experience to navigating a suspension bridge-requiring constant adaptation amid instability. These findings highlight the need for holistic diabetes care that addresses both medical and social dimensions, especially during times of crisis. This study reveals diabetes burnout as a critical but often overlooked barrier to effective diabetes management. Disruptions in daily routines, compounded by crises, heighten burnout risks. Aligning with global health policy benchmarks, our findings support the need for integrated care that addresses both medical and psychosocial aspects of diabetes. Health systems should prioritize mental health support, routine stability, and access to essential resources to improve long-term outcomes for people with type 1 diabetes.

papers.title: Tiredness and the Capacity to Decide: The Example of Maternity Care.
papers.abstract: Tiredness is taken seriously in healthcare where clinicians are concerned since good decisions require the ability to think clearly. The impact of patient tiredness is neglected. This is surprising, as there are healthcare contexts, like maternity care, where tiredness is nearly ubiquitous. Empirical research into sleep deprivation suggests that tiredness undermines substantially our abilities to understand and reason about potential choices. Since these abilities are necessary components of having capacity, tired patients may lack capacity in moments when important choices have to be made, for example a late intervention in active labour. I defend this argument. Tiredness can sometimes impair capacity and so justifies testing for capacity in some cases. Taking tiredness seriously and assessing it in practice is not paternalistic. Indeed, I argue that recognising the impact of tiredness, while failing to act on that fact, constitutes 'dependency denial' which harms women in maternity care.

papers.title: Sleep-disordered breathing in children with class II and large overjet treated with removable functional appliance - A longitudinal study.
papers.abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) was examined in children aged 9-14 years with class II and large overjet ≥ 6 mm (study group) before (T0), during (T1) and after treatment (T2) with a removable functional appliance, compared to a control group. At T0, the study group included 37 children, and the control group included 32 children. For both groups, exclusion criteria were as follows: diseases, syndromes, allergies, asthma, mouth breathing, adenoid vegetations, and hypertrophied tonsils. SDB was assessed and scored manually by respiratory polygraphy. SDB parameters between the groups were compared using a general linear model adjusted for sex, treatment time, and body mass index. No significant difference in SDB was found between the groups (p = .258), although at T0, 8.6% of the children in the study group and none in the control group had SDB. None were diagnosed with SDB at T1 or T2. No significant differences in changes in SDB parameters between the groups were observed from T0-T1, T1-T2, or T0-T2. At T0, 8.6% of study group children had SDB but none at T1 or T2. No significant difference in changes in SDB parameters over time was found between the groups. NCT04964830.

papers.title: One Step at a Time: Design and Rationale for Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trials.
papers.abstract: Stepped-wedge cluster randomized trials provide researchers with an opportunity to simultaneously implement and evaluate systemic interventions in real-world settings. This study design may have advantages compared with other cluster randomized trial (CRT) designs by optimizing feasibility and uptake when resources or personnel are limited. We present strengths, limitations, and key considerations when deciding whether to use a stepped-wedge design. Statistical analysis of stepped-wedge trials differs from that of traditional CRTs and should account for changes in outcome measures due to the intervention separate from those due to secular or time-based trends. We conclude with an example of a stepped-wedge study at 26 hospitals that helped to establish the effectiveness and safety of the Eat, Sleep, Console approach to neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome.

papers.title: Determination of the Presence of Daridorexant, a New Hypnotic, in Hair After a Single Exposure and Application to Repetitive Exposures.
papers.abstract: Daridorexant, a new hypnotic used to treat chronic insomnia in adults, has been marketed in France since March 2024. It is an orexin receptor antagonist that blocks orexin binding and promotes sleep without disrupting the natural sleep cycle. Daridorexant could be a good candidate for drug-facilitated crimes; however, to date, this has never been observed in such cases. This study aimed to identify daridorexant in hair. A healthy male volunteer ingested a single 25-mg daridorexant tablet. Two locks of light-brown hair were collected 4 weeks later. After incubation at a basic pH and extraction using an appropriate solvent mixture, daridorexant was analyzed using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (TSQ Altis Plus, Thermo Fisher Scientific). In the segment corresponding to the exposure time, daridorexant concentration was 0.029 pg/mg. The other segments were negative. To expand the detectability data for this molecule, a second study was conducted after repeated consumption of 25 mg daridorexant over 6 days. The results obtained are consistent with the findings of the first study, with a response at 0.8 pg/mg in the segment of interest. Furthermore, hair analysis of an assault victim revealed the presence of daridorexant at 35 pg/mg. In this case, the victim voluntarily consumed the prescribed daridorexant for 2 months after the assault to aid sleep. The authors report, for the first time, quantitative data on daridorexant detection in hair after single and repeated exposures. The test results are difficult to interpret because they represent the first data available in the literature. Nevertheless, the use of a sensitive analytical system, such as liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, seems necessary given the very low concentrations measured.

papers.title: International Survey of Growth Hormone and Sleep Evaluation Practices in Infants With Prader-Willi Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Guidelines encourage polysomnogram (PSG) prior to starting growth hormone (GH) in individuals with Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS) to avoid adverse effects; however, this presents a challenge in infancy due to barriers regarding access and lack of normative data to guide recommendations. This international survey study assessed clinician practices regarding GH initiation and sleep evaluation in infants with PWS. The primary objective was to determine the prevalence of clinicians reporting they do not always perform a baseline PSG prior to GH Initiation and whether responses were associated with volume of PWS patients seen annually. A survey was distributed through 10 medical societies involved in PWS care. Respondents were grouped by volume of patients with PWS seen annually (<5 (low volume, LV), 5-20 (medium volume, MV), and >/= 21 (high volume, HV) and practice region (United States (US) vs. outside of the US). The primary outcome was evaluated using bivariate analysis, a test for trend, and multivariable logistic regression. All other outcome analyses were considered exploratory. We analysed 141 surveys from 18 countries (primarily US respondents; 79%). There were 58 (41%) LV, 42 (30%) MV, and 41 (29%) HV respondents. With respect to our primary outcome, HV respondents were more likely to answer "not always" when asked whether they perform baseline PSG prior to GH initiation with a decreasing trend to the LV group (HV: 56%, MV: 31%, LV: 26%, p = 0.003). Concurrently, the most common reason to forgo the baseline PSG in the US is to avoid delaying GH start (56%) and less concerns about side effects (apnea, sudden death) in this age group (54%). Outside of the US, the top reason was lack of availability of sleep lab (78%). In multivariable logistic regression, the odds of "not always" obtaining a baseline PSG prior to starting GH in infants was 3.66 times (95% CI: 1.48, 9.04) higher in individuals seeing more than 21 PWS patients (HV) compared to less than 5 (LV) when controlling for respondent's geographic location and years treating patients with PWS (p = 0.004). High volume PWS clinicians were more likely to report not always obtaining baseline PSG prior to starting GH in infants, primarily to prevent delayed therapy. These findings highlight a gap between guidelines and practice and support the need for prospective outcome data.

papers.title: Characteristics, Risk Factors, and Long-Term Outcomes of Dysphagia Following Modified Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty: A Mixed-Methods Study.
papers.abstract: Modified Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (mUPPP) is a standard surgical intervention for Obstructive Sleep Apnea Hypopnea Syndrome (OSAHS), but postoperative dysphagia remains an underdiagnosed and poorly managed complication due to the lack of standardised assessment protocols. This prospective mixed-methods observational study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics, independent risk factors, and long-term outcomes of dysphagia following mUPPP. A prospective observational study was conducted on 120 OSAHS patients undergoing mUPPP. A mixed-methods assessment (EAT-10, interviews, and FEES) was performed at 2 weeks, 1, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to identify independent risk factors. The rate of patients screening positive for clinically significant dysphagia symptoms (EAT-10 ≥ 3, patient-reported screening threshold) was 63.3% at 2 weeks postoperatively. FEES confirmed pathological swallowing abnormalities, such as delayed pharyngeal response and aspiration risk, in over 94% of EAT-10-positive patients. Four independent risk factors were identified: female gender, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), anxiety/depression, and excessive daytime sleepiness (ESS ≥ 10). Symptoms persisted in approximately 19.2% of patients at 6 months and 9.2% at 12 months, with patients having multiple risk factors showing a significantly higher risk of long-term persistence. Dysphagia is a common and persistent sequela following mUPPP. The combination of EAT-10 and FEES is recommended for comprehensive postoperative monitoring. Preoperative identification and management of risk factors (gender, GERD, psychological status, and sleepiness) are crucial for risk stratification and implementing personalised interventions to reduce the burden of persistent dysphagia.

papers.title: [One anastomosis mini gastric bypass in patients with severe obesity].
papers.abstract: To evaluate the results of one anastomosis mini-gastric bypass in surgical treatment of severe obesity. This study presents the results of a 3-year follow-up of 17 patients who underwent mini-gastric bypass surgery. Their age ranged from 27 to 60 years (median 47.0). Preoperative BMI was 64.28 kg/m² (range 60.0-83.66). The follow-up examinations were conducted at 1 week, 3, 6, 12, 24 and 36 months after surgery. We assessed anthropometric data (BMI, excess weight loss - EWL, total weight loss - TWL), glycose metabolism parameters, lipid profile, blood pressure and therapy. Preoperative body weight was 186.1 kg [159; 230], TWL - 37.6 kg [23; 67], EWL - 57.3 kg [36; 90]. According to our study, remission of diabetes occurred in 84% of cases, sleep apnea symptoms regressed in 94.1% of cases. Normal blood pressure or reduced need for medications was achieved in 50% of cases. Normalization of low-density lipoproteins or statin dose reduction occurred in 79% of cases. Thus, mini-gastric bypass is a relatively safe procedure with minimal rate of early postoperative complications.

papers.title: Unpacking the Obesity Paradox in Lung Cancer: A Nationwide Analysis of In-Hospital Mortality From the US National Inpatient Sample (2020-2022).
papers.abstract: Background Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Although obesity is an established risk factor for multiple malignancies, numerous studies have reported an "obesity paradox," wherein patients with obesity demonstrate improved survival compared with normal-weight or underweight individuals. Whether this survival advantage reflects a true protective biological mechanism or methodological artifacts such as reverse causation driven by cancer cachexia and selection bias remains controversial, particularly within the acute inpatient setting. We evaluated the independent association between documented obesity and in-hospital mortality among lung cancer hospitalizations. Methods We performed a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the US National Inpatient Sample (2020-2022). Adult hospitalizations (age ≥18 years) with a diagnosis of lung cancer were identified and dichotomized by the presence or absence of an International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) obesity code; the unit of analysis was the hospitalization rather than the individual patient, and the exposure was documented obesity coding rather than measured adiposity. Baseline demographics, comorbidities, and in-hospital complications were compared using the chi-squared test (categorical variables) and the Mann-Whitney U test (continuous variables). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and hospital-level covariates. Results Of 61,963 unweighted lung cancer hospitalizations, 7,065 (11.4%) carried an obesity code. Obese patients were younger (median: 68 vs. 70 years) and more often female (4,090/7,065 (57.9%) vs. 28,011/54,898 (51%)). They had a higher prevalence of hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea (1,703 (24.1%) vs. 2,910 (5.3%)) but a lower weighted Elixhauser score (median: 10 vs. 16). In-hospital mortality was lower in the obese group (278 (3.9%) vs. 3,746 (6.8%); p<0.001). After adjustment, an obesity code was independently associated with 33% lower odds of in-hospital death (adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 0.67; 95% CI: 0.58-0.77; p<0.001). Conclusions Documented obesity coding was independently associated with lower in-hospital mortality among lung cancer hospitalizations. However, the low sensitivity of administrative obesity coding, a binary exposure that cannot separate normal-weight from cachectic patients, and the susceptibility of hospitalized cohorts to collider and reverse-causation bias mean this association should not be interpreted as a protective effect of adiposity. The paradox is most parsimoniously explained by confounding by illness severity rather than a therapeutic target, and the finding should be interpreted as an association involving documented obesity coding rather than an effect of adiposity itself.

papers.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Pain Chronification: Neuroimmune Rationale, Evidence Boundaries, and Trial Design Priorities: A Structured Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Pain chronification is a dynamic transition in which persistent pain may be shaped by interacting nociceptive, peripheral, spinal, supraspinal, neuroimmune, endocrine and cognitive-affective processes. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) has clinical value in chronic pain, but claims about glial modulation and disease modification require careful qualification. To evaluate CBT as an early, mechanism-informed and hypothesis-generating intervention while distinguishing clinical efficacy, neuroimmune plausibility, prevention hypotheses and disease-modifying claims. We conducted a structured narrative review using prespecified evidence domains. PubMed/MEDLINE searches covering January 2014 to September 10, 2026 were complemented by citation chasing and selected landmark mechanistic articles. Sources were organized by evidence domain, study type and interpretive role, including pain chronification, neuroimmune and glial mechanisms, brain-network mechanisms, CBT outcomes, psychoneuroimmune pathways, perioperative prevention hypotheses, risk phenotyping and scalable delivery. No quantitative pooling or formal systematic/scoping-review workflow was performed. Experimental and translational studies support neuroimmune contributions to central sensitization and pain maintenance, whereas human evidence for direct CBT effects on microglial or astrocytic activation remains insufficient. CBT produces reproducible, generally small effects on pain intensity and more consistent benefits for interference, disability, distress, coping, sleep and function. CBT should be presented as a clinically valuable component of multimodal care and as a testable psychoneuroimmune hypothesis, not as a proven preventive, glial-targeting or disease-modifying treatment. Risk-stratified, early, component-specific and mechanism-embedded trials are needed before prevention claims are made.

papers.title: A serum cytokine-derived integrated inflammatory profile score (IIPS) links systemic inflammation to symptom burden and severity in COPD.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic inflammatory syndrome in which forced expiratory volume in 1 s expressed as a percentage of predicted value (FEV1% predicted) may dissociate from patient-reported symptom burden. This study evaluated an Integrated Inflammatory Profile Score (IIPS) as a potential biological correlate for a more holistic assessment of stable COPD. Serum concentrations of 11 cytokines were measured in 62 patients with stable COPD. The IIPS was derived using automated linear modeling with forward stepwise selection guided by the corrected Akaike information criterion (AICc). Associations of the IIPS with COPD Assessment Test (CAT) scores were compared with those of FEV1% predicted. The optimized IIPS, comprising interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), interleukin-2 (IL-2), and interleukin-10 (IL-10), was significantly associated with FEV1% predicted (R2 = 0.1867, p = 0.0005) and outperformed the individual cytokines in discriminating spirometric severity (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) = 0.7381). For symptom burden, FEV1% predicted showed greater explanatory power for exertional domains, particularly breathlessness (R2 = 0.0832) and activities (R2 = 0.1280). By contrast, the IIPS showed numerically stronger trend-level associations for sleep (R2 = 0.0519, p = 0.0750) and energy (R2 = 0.0511, p = 0.0773), although these associations did not reach conventional statistical significance. The IIPS reflects Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD)-defined physiological severity more effectively than any single cytokine measured in this study. Its associations with patient-reported systemic symptoms were modest and exploratory, suggesting that integrated inflammatory profiling may complement spirometry in characterizing COPD burden but requires external and longitudinal validation before clinical application.
